good_thing: (San Mateo County, California): The San Francisco Zoo and conservation partners released 62 young San Francisco garter snakes at carefully selected wild sites this autumn. Biologists had temporarily brought pregnant females from a healthy population to the zoo, raised the offspring through their most vulnerable stage, and genetically tested each juvenile before release. The zoo calls it the first successful head-starting program for this endangered snake, found only in a small part of the Bay Area.
current_or_history: On November 23, 1889, San Francisco’s Palais Royale Saloon put two coin-operated phonographs into public use, an early step toward the jukebox. They had listening tubes rather than speakers, so customers leaned in to hear a recording through one of the attached tubes. Public recorded music began as a surprisingly private little experience.
tiny_fact: Wombats really do produce cube-shaped droppings. Research found that the cubes form in the last part of the intestine, where alternating tissue stiffness and contractions make flat faces and corners as the material dries and firms.
